$comment: The contract inventory. Spec Testing item 1, implementation Task 0.5.
THE GATE IS THIS FILE, NOT THE ASSERTION TOTAL. The spike settled that
empirically rather than by argument: tools/scoring.test.mjs reported
`1535 passed, 0 failed` while running against a public suffix list that had
been silently swapped underneath it, and the count was byte-identical to the
correct baseline. A number that cannot notice that is not a coverage signal.
So: every area below must have a passing suite; the total is REPORTED beside
it as a tripwire; and no entry is removed without a stated replacement.
A decrease in a suite's count must name the assertions removed and where the
Enforced by tests/contract/inventory.test.mjs, which runs each suite and
compares what it printed against what is recorded here.

baseline.note: The pre-refactor total, from the spec's baseline table. Reproduced on 2026-08-27.

suites.note: Reports findings rather than an assertion count, which is why it has no number. Stays in npm test: it is the only thing that catches src/data/locales-en.js drifting from locales/en.json, and Phase 2 changed that file's format, which is exactly the drift it exists to catch.

every Content-Security-Policy directive in index.html

booleans, nullability and absence

states unreachable through analyzeDomain, each with its structural reason
the issue vocabulary closes against locales/en.json at 106 tokens
determinism of the canonical form
array order, absence versus undefined, tagged non-JSON primitives
values refused at the result surface: functions, symbols, cycles
no empty value is dropped and no float is rounded
the query trace's stated tolerance, and the counts it must not cost
CSV as exact bytes
the DOM tree and its line form, proven equally sensitive
the report's byte-exact policy and stylesheet regions
exclusions: per-field, reasoned, no wildcards
each rule's NEGATIVE case — the difference it exists to catch
every registry member has exactly one coverage row
every row names a suite or corpus case that exists
every non-enum shape names its axes and its cases
the extracted-module comparison: what src/ exports must match the registry
the targeted legacy contracts are wired
the legacy entry point has no exports, which is what keeps globalName safe to omit
src/data/ is a sink: the generated tables import nothing and export exactly one table each
every adapter carries the LEGACY_ADAPTER sentinel, and the remaining count is reported
the import-graph FLOOR is defined mechanically: src/data/ and src/platform/ import nothing, and a file that grows an import rejoins the state comparison
the 24-name global inventory is closed

the marked adapters are named, and the remaining count is reported
the scan catches window, globalThis and self, and ignores comments and same-named locals
what still reaches for globals under js/ is counted, so a phase that adds one is visible
the §11 primitive set is complete, checked against the module's own declaration
language built-ins are required APIs, not injected services
every method keeps its receiver when destructured off the platform, proven against a window that refuses unbound calls
host objects are passed whole and constructors come from the window
a platform is per runtime: two calls share nothing and one window's calls do not reach another
now() and formatDateTime() preserve the v0.5.0 call and are pinnable by the window's clock
src/platform/ imports nothing and never reaches for the ambient window
importing src/runtime.js performs no DOM, network or global work, asserted in a process with no browser
it constructs nothing at module scope and reads no ambient global
the runtime carries the two supported facade members plus the Phase 2 parts
generated data reaches the engine and the fixture table is the one in force
ONE runtime holds ONE DoH cache with page lifetime: a sibling audit reuses the walk
two runtimes share nothing, and isolation comes from constructing rather than from cache-busting an import
the facade delegates to the engine, including a core transport failure
the artifact under test is the one index.html names and _site publishes
the built artifact creates the same 24 globals as the source, and introduces none of its own
DnsAudit's 95 members and __APP_TEST__ match between source and bundle
WEIGHTS, PARKED_WEIGHTS, GRADE_THRESHOLDS and POLICY_RANK are byte-identical
generated data survived bundling: the whole PSL, the catalog, and the inlined English bundle

an altered artifact fails the comparison, and an extra global is caught
the exact top-level _site allowlist, asserted as a set
absence: src, tools, tests, docs, node_modules, js, assets, package files, AGENTS.md
absence by pattern at any depth: test files, stray source maps, markdown, translation-status.json
every script, stylesheet and source-map reference resolves inside _site
co-location safety bound to metafile.inputs and the source map's sources, not to a sentinel
no third-party JavaScript and no cross-origin reference at the delivery boundary
the allowlist and the pattern scans are each shown to catch an addition
the runner is deterministic across two runs of one root
each of the five surfaces distinguishes cases
seven mutations, rebuilt into the artifact and each caught on the surfaces it should be and no others
a subject is a complete root: a stylesheet-only edit moves the report
a script listed in index.html but absent is refused, not skipped
a subject whose generated data was substituted is refused, not measured
a mutation that is NOT rebuilt moves nothing — the control that proves the rebuild is what makes section 2 work
the subject manifest is complete: every script, stylesheet and index.html hashed, and nothing else
re-reading one subject produces identical hashes, and a one-byte change moves one
module evaluation order: the entry installs before it imports its consumers

notInNpmTest.why: The five-surface comparison against the committed baseline. 38 s for 30 cases, so it runs at every phase gate rather than inside npm test. Framework §3's 'move it to every commit' reading was based on an 8-case corpus and was revised when the corpus was completed.
areas: five-surface equivalence against v0.5.0: result, query trace, CSV, HTML report, DOM

notInNpmTest.why: Drives a real headless browser at a real file:// URL. Kept out of npm test so a missing browser is one clearly-named failure rather than a broken suite -- but it REFUSES to skip, so it can never pass without having run. CI runs it as its own job, and it is a Gate 1 acceptance criterion.
areas: the page loads from file:// with one classic script and no module
the application initialises: 24 globals, DnsAudit at 95 members, the whole PSL
i18n resolves from the INLINED English bundle, with no network available
real computation runs: the PSL-reading org-domain walk and the DER key walk

notInNpmTest.why: Regenerates the measured coverage columns of tests/state-matrix.json. Run when the corpus or the registry changes; state-matrix.test.mjs is what gates the result.
areas: corpus coverage measurement

notInNpmTest.why: Live DNS. A local grade-DISTRIBUTION check and never a gate, never the equivalence oracle.
